blocks: Blue Book: Comprehensive Dog Population Management Training Guide

This Blue Book provides a definitive framework for Lucknow Nagar Nigam in developing and implementing systematic training programmes for Humane Animal Population Control. The guide outlines critical methodologies for creating effective training modules, conducting hands-on practical sessions, and ensuring participant competency in advanced animal welfare and population control techniques.

The document is meticulously crafted to standardise approaches to dog population management, emphasising humane practices, scientific methodologies, and community-centered interventions. It serves as an essential resource for municipal administrators, veterinary professionals, and field workers engaged in animal population control initiatives.
Ensuring consistent quality of animal population management interventions
Promoting humane and scientific approaches to dog population control

The successful implementation of the Animal Birth Control Training Programme hinges on a collaborative approach involving multiple key stakeholders, each with clearly defined roles and responsibilities.

The Lucknow Nagar Nigam shall serve as the administrative authority responsible for ensuring the establishment, maintenance, and oversight of essential infrastructural and logistical units required for effective programme implementation and through the Municipal Veterinary Officer (MVO) serve as the central coordinating body, ensuring strategic alignment and operational excellence throughout the programme's lifecycle. The MVO will be responsible for overseeing day to day management, facilitating collaboration with Training agency, ensuring adherence with these bluebook guidelines and maintaining rigorous documentation of programme progress. The MVO will prepare and submit detailed quarterly reports to the Uttar Pradesh Animal Birth Control Monitoring Committee, providing transparent insights into programme implementation, challenges, and achievements. The MVO, with the help of the Training Agency, will be responsible for managing application processes, addressing technical queries, and ensuring smooth programme implementation.

Training Agency: The Designated Training Agency will function as the programme's operational core, bearing direct responsibility for curriculum development, participant management, practical training execution, maintaining meticulous records, and providing regular progress reports to the Nagar Nigam. Given that the training facility is located within the existing ABC centre, the agency implementing the ABC programme at the centre shall be designated as the Training Agency.
Uttar Pradesh Animal Birth Control Monitoring Committee:

Uttar Pradesh Animal Birth Control Monitoring Committee will provide critical oversight and strategic guidance through its dedicated sub-committee. This committee will conduct comprehensive quarterly reviews, evaluate programme effectiveness, and make informed recommendations for continuous improvement. Their role extends beyond mere monitoring to active programme refinement, ensuring alignment with emerging best practices in animal welfare and population management.
Animal Welfare Board of India: The Board will rigorously review and approve the training curriculum, ensuring it meets national standards for humane animal population control.
Additionally, the Board will collaborate with Lucknow Nagar Nigam to issue official certificates of completion to participants who successfully demonstrate the required competence

Programme participants: Participants will comprise a diverse cohort including veterinary professionals, para-veterinary personnel, animal handlers, programme managers from animal welfare organisations, and government officials. This multidisciplinary approach ensures a comprehensive understanding of canine population management strategies.

Important Note: A comprehensive Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) will be executed between Lucknow Nagar Nigam and the Training Agency. This document will delineate roles, responsibilities, operational protocols, and collaborative mechanisms, providing a clear institutional framework for programme execution.

The financial governance of the ABC Training Programme will be overseen by the sub-committee constituted by the State Animal Birth Control Monitoring committee. This committee shall be responsible for fixing the rate of participant fee and determining the remuneration to be paid to the Training Agency for each batch of trainees.
The responsibilities of the Sub-Committee shall include:
Development of cost per participant for training.

To ensure that the fee paid by the participants and any reimbursement received from the State Government or Animal Welfare Board of India or any other agency, towards ABC Training shall be deposited in the …… bank account. In the books maintained by the Lucknow Nagar Nigam specific accounting heads shall be created for:

Creation of utilisation plan for surplus revenue generated through the programme towards improvement of the training centre. These funds will be systematically used into enhancing training infrastructure, upgrading programme methodologies, and improving overall programme capabilities.
The accounting of the ABC training programme shall be distinct from the ongoing ABC programme and income and expenditure for each shall be accounted for separately.

The fee structures and financial parameters established by the sub-committee will require formal approval from the Municipal Commissioner of Lucknow Nagar Nigam. These financial provisions will be subject to annual review and revision.
The financial management framework shall aim to balance three critical objectives:
Generating resources for continuous programme improvement

This institutional communication strategy encompasses a strategic outreach methodology designed to engage key stakeholders across multiple governmental and non-governmental domains.
The initial communication phase shall entail targeted official correspondence dispatched to the following institutional entities:
Uttar Pradesh State Animal Welfare Board

Candidate Screening and Document Verification: A two member team consisting of the Municipal Veterinary officer and an officer nominated by the Training Agency is to be created for the purpose of screening and document verification of participants. The screening and document verification should be done based on a checklist [Annexure C]. After verification the committee needs to ensure apprising the selected candidates via email and phone, asking them to deposit a fee within a specified period of time.

Payment of Fees: Upon confirmation the selected candidates are to pay the requisite course fee payment through online bank transfer to the designated account, demand draft in favour of "....", or digital payment through authorised payment gateways. The fee structure varies by category for veterinarians, para-vets, and handlers. Upon successful payment verification, a system-generated receipt with a unique transaction ID will be issued that includes participant details, payment amount, mode of payment, and date.

Issuance of Confirmation Letter: Following payment verification, a formal course confirmation letter will be issued by the Municipal Veterinary Officer via email. Thereby, a participant register [Annexure D] is to be created and maintained by the Training Agency. The Training Agency will then keep the selected participants apprised of the date and venue related queries and any other details that the participants may require.

Undertaking signed by the participant for following prescribed safety protocols

These protocols are essential to ensure the safety and health of all participants—veterinarians, para-veterinarians, animal handlers, and other staff—at the training centre. These guidelines must be strictly followed to minimise risks of injury, infection, and disease transmission.
Pre-Exposure Rabies Vaccination: All participants must have received pre-exposure rabies vaccination. Proof of up-to-date vaccination should be presented before beginning the programme.
Tetanus Vaccination: A current tetanus vaccine is mandatory for all participants.
All participants must wear appropriate gears, including gloves, face masks, as and when required, while handling dogs or cleaning kennels.
Veterinarians and surgical assistants must follow surgical hand preparation protocols [scrub] as instructed by the lead trainer.
All para-veterinarians, handlers and programme managers must ensure that surfaces, kennels, and equipment are thoroughly cleaned and disinfected between uses.
All participants must dispose of single-use gloves and masks properly. All animal waste, soiled materials, and other biological waste in designated biohazard disposal bins.
Participants must report and immediately address any bites, scratches, or other injuries.
No participant shall, without supervision, approach any dog isolated for reason of illness or observation.
The undersigned agrees that s/he shall adhere strictly to all the prescribed safety protocols, as well as any safety measures announced or as instructed by the Lead Trainer.
